input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need anything else from me?

Yes, I can make regular calls and send normal text messages just fine. I’m actually in France right now, so I’m outside my usual area. As for the mobile data, I’m not really sure how to check if I’m connected to that instead of Wi-Fi. Could you tell me how to find out?
I checked, and it looks like there’s no signal and mobile data is disabled on my phone right now. What should I do next?
I just checked again, and Airplane Mode isn’t on. I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?
Alright, if you’re sure it won’t erase anything, I’ll go ahead and restart my phone. Should I check the signal and data icons again after it turns back on?
My phone has restarted, but I still don’t see any signal bars, and it looks like mobile data is still disabled. What should I try next?
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what to do about that—could you walk me through what I should try next?
Alright, I’ve reinserted the SIM card and turned my phone back on. Now I see a signal bar, but it says “2G” and mobile data still looks disabled. What should I do next?
I changed the network mode, and now it shows a strong signal with “5G,” but mobile data still looks disabled. What should I do now?
Okay, I turned on mobile data and now I see the “5G” icon with a strong signal. But I still can’t send picture messages—my messaging app says it can’t send MMS. What should I try next?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or should I try resetting these settings? I’m not sure what any of this means.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. It says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. Is it safe to restart again? I just want to make sure I won’t lose anything important.
I restarted my phone after resetting the APN settings, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t this working yet? Is there anything else we can try?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off and then try sending a picture message again?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried again, but I still can’t send picture messages. What should I check next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has access to storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Could that be the problem? What should I do next?
I was able to enable the SMS permission for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry this might never work.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture message) issue. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any service or data issues that might be affecting MMS. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need anything else from me?

Thank you for providing your information. I have identified your account. To help you send MMS (picture messages), I’ll need to check a few things about your service and data connection.

Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send text messages?
- Are you currently connected to mobile data (not just Wi-Fi)?
- Are you traveling outside your usual area or country?

This will help me guide you through the right troubleshooting steps.

Yes, I can make regular calls and send normal text messages just fine. I’m actually in France right now, so I’m outside my usual area. As for the mobile data, I’m not really sure how to check if I’m connected to that instead of Wi-Fi. Could you tell me how to find out?

Thank you for the details. Since you’re in France (outside your home network), MMS requires both mobile data and international roaming to be enabled on your line. I’ll check if your line is set up for roaming.

Meanwhile, to check if you’re connected to mobile data:
1. Look at the top of your phone’s screen (the status bar).
2. If you see icons like “4G,” “5G,” “LTE,” or “H+,” you’re connected to mobile data.
3. If you see a Wi-Fi symbol, you’re connected to Wi-Fi instead.

If you’re not sure, let me know what icons you see at the top of your screen, and I can help interpret them.

I’ll now check if your line is roaming enabled.

Please do the following steps:
1. Turn off Airplane Mode if it’s on.
2. Make sure mobile data is enabled on your phone.
3. Try sending your picture message (MMS) again.

If it still doesn’t work, let me know what icons you see at the top of your phone’s screen, and I’ll guide you through the next steps.

I checked, and it looks like there’s no signal and mobile data is disabled on my phone right now. What should I do next?

Since you have no signal and mobile data is disabled, let’s try to restore your connection. Please follow these steps:

1. Make sure Airplane Mode is OFF. If it’s on, turn it off.
2. If Airplane Mode is already off, try restarting your phone.
3. After restarting, check if you have any signal bars and if mobile data is enabled (look for “4G,” “5G,” “LTE,” or similar icons).

If you still have no signal after these steps, please let me know. If you see any error messages or unusual icons, describe them to me so I can assist you further.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I just checked again, and Airplane Mode isn’t on. I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?

Restarting your phone is a safe process and will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It simply refreshes your phone’s system and network connections, which can help restore your signal and mobile data.

Would you like to proceed with restarting your phone? If you have any concerns or need step-by-step instructions, let me know—I’m here to help!
Alright, if you’re sure it won’t erase anything, I’ll go ahead and restart my phone. Should I check the signal and data icons again after it turns back on?

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
My phone has restarted, but I still don’t see any signal bars, and it looks like mobile data is still disabled. What should I try next?

Thank you for restarting your phone. Since you still have no signal and mobile data is disabled, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Sometimes, the SIM card may not be properly seated, especially after traveling.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone:
- Go to your phone’s settings and look for “SIM status” or “About phone” > “SIM status.”
- Let me know if it says the SIM is “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.”

If you’re not sure how to check, or if you see “Missing” or “No SIM,” please let me know, and I’ll guide you through reseating your SIM card.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what to do about that—could you walk me through what I should try next?

Since your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, the next step is to reseat your SIM card. This means removing the SIM card from your phone and then reinserting it to ensure it’s properly connected.

Here’s how you can do it:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Locate the SIM card tray (usually on the side of your phone).
3. Use a SIM ejector tool or a small paperclip to gently open the tray.
4. Remove the SIM card, wait a few seconds, and then carefully reinsert it.
5. Close the tray and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if it now detects the SIM card and if you have signal bars. Let me know what you see, or if you need more detailed instructions for your specific phone model.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I’ve reinserted the SIM card and turned my phone back on. Now I see a signal bar, but it says “2G” and mobile data still looks disabled. What should I do next?

Great job reseating your SIM card! Now that you have a signal, let’s work on getting your mobile data working and improving your network connection.

Since your phone is showing “2G,” MMS may not work properly, and data speeds will be very slow. Here’s what to do next:

1. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if available).  
   - Go to your phone’s settings.
   - Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
   - Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
   - Select “4G/5G preferred” or “4G/3G/2G (auto connect).”

2. After changing the network mode, check if your phone connects to a faster network (like 4G or 5G) and if mobile data becomes enabled.

Let me know if you see the network change or if you need step-by-step instructions for your phone model. If mobile data is still disabled after this, please let me know.

Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode, and now it shows a strong signal with “5G,” but mobile data still looks disabled. What should I do now?

Now that you have a strong “5G” signal, the next step is to enable mobile data on your phone. Here’s how you can do it:

1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Select “Mobile Network.”
4. Find the option for “Mobile Data” and make sure it is turned ON.

After enabling mobile data, check if you see the mobile data icon (such as “5G,” “4G,” or “LTE” without a small “x” or “!”) and try sending your MMS again.

Let me know if mobile data is now enabled or if you encounter any issues turning it on.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Okay, I turned on mobile data and now I see the “5G” icon with a strong signal. But I still can’t send picture messages—my messaging app says it can’t send MMS. What should I try next?

Thank you for the update. Since you now have a strong 5G signal and mobile data is enabled, but MMS still won’t send, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues, especially when traveling internationally.

Please follow these steps:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Select “Mobile Network,” then “Access Point Names” (APN).
4. Check if there is an APN set, and if there is an “MMSC” or “MMS” URL listed.

If you’re not sure what you’re seeing, let me know. If the APN or MMSC is missing or looks incorrect, I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or should I try resetting these settings? I’m not sure what any of this means.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name and MMSC URL you provided look generally correct, but sometimes issues can still occur if other APN details are missing or misconfigured, especially after traveling internationally.

To ensure everything is set up correctly, I recommend resetting your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. This often resolves MMS issues.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you already know how to do this? After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

APN settings will reset at reboot.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. It says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. Is it safe to restart again? I just want to make sure I won’t lose anything important.

Yes, it is completely safe to restart your phone. Restarting will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other important data. It simply refreshes your phone’s system and applies the new APN settings.

Please go ahead and restart your phone. After it turns back on, try sending a picture message (MMS) again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble. I’m here to help until it’s resolved!

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since you still can’t send MMS after enabling roaming, reseating your SIM, changing network mode, enabling mobile data, and resetting APN settings, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS, especially when abroad.
2. Does your messaging app have the necessary permissions (like access to storage and SMS)?

Let’s start by checking if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled. Could you check your phone’s settings for Wi-Fi Calling and let me know if it’s turned on? If it is, please try turning it off and then attempt to send an MMS again.

If Wi-Fi Calling is already off or turning it off doesn’t help, we’ll check your messaging app’s permissions next. Let me know what you find!
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off and then try sending a picture message again?

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling and then try sending a picture message (MMS) again. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS, especially when you’re abroad.

After you turn it off, let me know if you’re able to send the MMS successfully or if you still encounter any issues. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll check your messaging app’s permissions next.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried again, but I still can’t send picture messages. What should I check next?

Thank you for trying that step. The next thing to check is whether your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS, specifically access to storage and SMS.

Please do the following:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Locate your messaging app (it may be called “Messages” or “Messaging”).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Make sure permissions for “Storage” and “SMS” are enabled.

If either of these permissions is not enabled, please turn them on and then try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if both permissions were already enabled, or if enabling them solves the issue. If it still doesn’t work, please let me know, and we’ll continue troubleshooting.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has access to storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Could that be the problem? What should I do next?

Yes, not having SMS permission enabled for your messaging app can prevent it from sending MMS (picture messages). Please check if there is an option to enable SMS permission for your messaging app. Sometimes, it may be listed as “Send and view SMS messages” or similar.

If you do not see an option for SMS permission:
- Try looking under “Advanced” or “Additional permissions” in the app’s permissions settings.
- If you still can’t find it, your phone may manage SMS permissions differently, or another app may be set as the default SMS app.

Please also check:
1. Is your messaging app set as the default SMS app? If not, set it as the default and try again.
2. If you find the SMS permission, enable it and then try sending an MMS.

Let me know if you’re able to enable SMS permission or set your messaging app as the default SMS app, and if that resolves the issue. If not, please tell me what options you see, and I’ll guide you further.

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I was able to enable the SMS permission for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry this might never work.

Thank you for enabling the SMS permission and for your patience throughout this process. You’ve already tried all the main troubleshooting steps for MMS issues, including:

- Enabling international roaming
- Reseating your SIM card
- Changing network mode to 4G/5G
- Enabling mobile data
- Resetting APN settings and restarting your phone
- Turning off Wi-Fi Calling
- Ensuring your messaging app has storage and SMS permissions

Since the issue still persists after all these steps, this may indicate a more complex technical problem that requires advanced support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate this further and provide specialized assistance.
